page: Microsoft Azure F32as_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The instance is allocated 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, maintaining a single-thread-per-core configuration that avoids resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128 GB of RAM, equating to 4 GB per core. The hardware architecture incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate high computational throughput. The instance achieved a top-decile Geekbench multi-core score of 21,998 and top-decile image processing performance. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 98,484.8, while PassMark CPU and database operation scores ranked in the top quartile. The presence of AVX-512 BF16 and VNNI supports CPU-bound machine learning tasks, demonstrated by small-model LLM prompt processing reaching 4,650.76 tokens per second. Memory throughput remains robust for cached small-block reads, although uncached large-block reads and gzip compression fall closer to median infrastructure tiers.

The F32as_v6 includes no bundled local storage and features zero integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached remote disks such as Azure Premium Storage. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides greater RAM density than traditional 1:2 compute-optimized instances while delivering dedicated per-core compute capacity. This architectural balance eliminates noisy-neighbor core sharing, making it suitable for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration software builds, video and image processing pipelines, batch data transformations, and high-concurrency Redis caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure F32as_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 128 GB of system memory, the instance delivers 4 GB of RAM per core with single-thread-per-core execution. The processor includes hardware vector support via AVX-512 extensions (VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core compute capability, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 21,998 and PassMark CPU score at 62,590.72. The instance contains no onboard local disks, relying on remote storage options like Azure Premium Storage, and carries no GPUs. Its resource profile is well-suited for high-throughput batch compilation, data transformations, image processing, and distributed in-memory caching workloads.
